choices: everyone in fact thinks in a private mental language before translating into public speech
sensations cannot exist unless they are named
the meaning of a word is the mental image it calls up in the speaker

a genuinely private language -- whose terms refer to sensations available only to the speaker -- is impossible, because correct use requires a criterion of correctness that a purely private rule cannot supply
explanation: Wittgenstein argues that without a public standard, 'seems right' and 'is right' collapse, so a genuinely private rule/language cannot secure meaning -- a challenge that also presses on any inner Mentalese. Option 0 is close to the LOT view he opposes; option 2 is the mental-image theory of meaning he criticises; option 1 misstates the conclusion.
